title: Cylinder 9 Injector Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher-than-expected voltage in the cylinder 9 fuel injector circuit. This usually points to an unplugged or broken circuit, or a wire shorted to power.
symptoms: Misfire, often with a cylinder 9 misfire code
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Open coil in the cylinder 9 injector
Faulty injector driver in the engine computer

checks: Make sure the injector connector is fully plugged in and its pins are clean
Measure the injector's resistance and check the wiring for breaks
fix: Usually reconnecting or repairing the injector wiring, or a new injector.

title: Cylinder 9 Contribution/Balance
plain: The computer compares how much each cylinder helps spin the engine. Cylinder 9 is doing noticeably more or less work than the others.
symptoms: Extra smoke from the exhaust on diesels

causes.name: Weak, leaking or clogged injector on cylinder 9
Ignition problem on that cylinder (gas engines)

checks: Run a cylinder balance or contribution test with a scan tool
Do a compression test on that cylinder
Inspect the injector connector and wiring
fix: Most often a new injector for that cylinder. A compression problem means deeper engine repair.

title: Cylinder 10 Injector Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower-than-expected voltage in the cylinder 10 fuel injector circuit. This usually points to a short to ground or a bad injector.
symptoms: Misfire, often with a cylinder 10 misfire code
Less power and worse fuel economy

causes.name: Shorted coil in the cylinder 10 injector
Faulty injector driver in the engine computer

checks: Measure the injector's resistance and compare it with the other injectors
Inspect the injector wiring for rubbing or melted insulation
fix: Usually a new injector or a wiring repair.

title: Vehicle Overspeed Condition
plain: The vehicle went faster than the top speed the computer is set to allow. The computer logs it and may cut power to slow the vehicle.
symptoms: Engine may cut power at high speed
Speedometer may read wrong if a sensor is the cause

causes.name: Vehicle actually exceeded its programmed speed limit, such as coasting downhill with a load
Wrong tire size or axle ratio programmed in the computer

checks: Check whether the speedometer reads correctly against GPS
Confirm the tire size and axle ratio settings match the vehicle
fix: If it was a real overspeed event, clear the code. Otherwise correct the tire size setting or replace a faulty speed sensor.

title: Engine Oil Over Temperature Condition
plain: The engine oil has gotten too hot. Overheated oil stops protecting the engine well and can lead to serious wear.
symptoms: Oil temperature warning or check engine light
Engine may cut power to protect itself

causes.name: Heavy towing or hard driving in hot weather
Clogged or failed engine oil cooler

checks: Pull over, let the engine cool and check the oil level
Check the coolant level and that the cooling fans work
Compare the oil temperature reading on a scan tool with a cold engine
fix: Depends on the cause: often topping up or changing the oil, or fixing the oil cooler or cooling system.
drive: Pull over when safe and shut the engine off. Overheated oil stops protecting the engine, and driving on can cause serious damage. Once it cools, check oil and coolant. If both are fine and the warning stays off, drive gently with no towing; if it comes back, have it towed.
test_first: Check oil and coolant levels, the cooling fans and the oil cooler, and compare the oil temperature reading with the real temperature on a cold engine to rule out a bad sensor first.

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger "A" Underboost Condition
plain: The turbo or supercharger isn't making as much boost pressure as the computer expects, so the engine has less power than it should.
symptoms: Noticeable loss of power or sluggish acceleration
Check engine light on, sometimes with limp mode
Whistling or hissing sound when accelerating
Worse fuel economy or black smoke on diesels

causes.name: Boost leak from a cracked intercooler hose, loose clamp or leaking intercooler
Wastegate stuck open or faulty boost control solenoid
Clogged air filter or restricted exhaust

checks: Listen for hissing and inspect the intercooler pipes, hoses and clamps
Have the intake smoke or pressure tested for boost leaks
Check the wastegate, its actuator and the boost control vacuum lines
fix: Most often a boost leak repair such as a new intercooler hose or clamp. Check the wastegate and boost control before blaming the turbo.

cost.job: Repair boost leak (intercooler hose or clamp)

examples: Frequently reported on VW and Audi 2.0L turbo engines
Also common on Ford EcoBoost engines and GM Duramax diesel trucks
drive: You can usually drive gently to a shop soon, but expect weak acceleration, so leave extra room when merging or passing. If you see heavy smoke, smell oil or hear grinding or a loud whine from the turbo, stop and get it checked first; a failing turbo can damage the engine.
test_first: Smoke or pressure test the intake for boost leaks, check the wastegate, boost control solenoid and vacuum lines, and check turbo shaft play before replacing the turbocharger.

title: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
plain: The computer is adding as much fuel as it's allowed to on cylinder 1, and that cylinder still seems to run lean (short on fuel).

causes.name: Vacuum leak near that cylinder's intake port

checks: Check for other fuel trim, misfire or fuel pressure codes
Have the cylinder 1 injector flow or balance tested
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the injector, or fixing a vacuum leak near that cylinder.

title: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Min Limit
plain: The computer is cutting as much fuel as it's allowed to on cylinder 1, and that cylinder still seems to run rich (too much fuel).
symptoms: Hard starting, fuel smell or black smoke

causes.name: Faulty oxygen or air-fuel sensor reading

checks: Check for other fuel trim, misfire or fuel pressure codes
Have the cylinder 1 injector flow or balance tested
fix: Usually a new injector for that cylinder after fuel pressure is confirmed good.

title: Cylinder 1 - Injector Restricted
plain: The computer thinks the cylinder 1 injector is partly clogged and not delivering enough fuel.

causes.name: Clogged injector from deposits or debris
Injector wiring problem making it open too little

checks: Check for other fuel trim, misfire or fuel pressure codes
Have the cylinder 1 injector flow or balance tested
fix: Usually a new injector, or professional cleaning on engines where that works.

title: Cylinder 1 - Injector Leaking
plain: The computer thinks the cylinder 1 injector is letting fuel through when it should be shut.
symptoms: Hard starting, fuel smell or black smoke

causes.name: Debris holding the injector partly open

checks: Check for other fuel trim, misfire or fuel pressure codes
Have the cylinder 1 injector flow or balance tested
fix: Usually a new injector for that cylinder. Fix it soon, since raw fuel can thin the oil and damage the catalytic converter.
